name: fixed-budget-search-curve-v1
question: Can a smaller forcing-search budget retain most of confirmed Forcing-3's strength gain?
domain: Development-only reuse of the 80 completed Forcing-3 confirmation games and their 20 opening pairs
formula: The accepted Locked-3 coefficients remain unchanged for every policy
policies: forcing-1-64: one forcing ply, 64 children per root, calibrated near 100 mean states
searched-3: two forcing plies, 128 children per root, calibrated near 300 mean states
forcing-3-128: three forcing plies, 128 children per root, calibrated near 1,000 mean states
forcing-3: confirmed three forcing plies, 256 children per root
forcing-4-256: four forcing plies, 256 children per root, calibrated near 3,000 mean states
position_sample: Three SHA-256 seed-ranked candidate turns per completed game after the eight-ply opening, deduplicated by rule state; at least 230 unique positions
oracle: Stockfish 18 depth 12 root and root-move-constrained scores, one thread, 16 MB hash
game_curve: Each non-anchor policy plays all 20 completed confirmation openings twice against the confirmed anchor with colors reversed; development only
metrics: mean, median, p95, and thresholded move regret
mean/p95/max states, cap binding, and wall time
opening-paired score and engine-pool Elo versus the confirmed anchor
decision: A cheaper policy is eligible only if it retains at least 80% of the anchor's regret gain over forcing-1-64, increases mean regret by at most 10 cp with bootstrap upper bound at most 15 cp, scores at least 47.5% against the anchor, and has a paired score lower bound at least 40%. Select at most one by lowest mean states, then regret, then label.
guardrail: All positions and openings are completed confirmation data reused for development. Any selected policy requires a newly frozen opening suite before a claim.
